title: Product Marginals and Density-Moment Thresholds for Ising Transfer Kernels
abstract: Fix a positive Ising coupling. We construct strictly positive weights on Boolean cubes whose labelled marginals on every set of at most a fixed positive fraction of coordinates equal uniform product marginals, while exponentially many normalized transfer eigenvalues approach one exponentially fast. The Perron stationary law has the same marginals. Binary codes, a positive product admixture and a finite block estimate supply the construction. A full parity-transfer spectrum separates this mechanism from heat-bath slowdown. Conversely, for Boolean noise parameter 0<rho<1, density moments of order s>(1+rho)/(1-rho) imply an explicit dimension-independent transfer gap, without pointwise upper or positive lower bounds and allowing zero weights. For every 1<s<(1+rho)/(1-rho) and B>1, antipodal product tilts and a Gram comparison yield normalized densities with Ls norm at most B and density at least 1/B whose gaps collapse exponentially. At the critical exponent, a sufficiently small moment budget gives an explicit gap without pointwise bounds, while every fixed budget B>2 admits positive densities bounded below by 1/B with stretched-exponentially collapsing gaps. The optimal critical budget remains open. The threshold and ingredients are classical; external priority of these joint spectral conclusions is unestablished. Global many-body weights are allowed; no fixed-range Gibbs or local-dynamics claim follows.
